claims.text: Smoke inhalation with CO: some authorities prefer hydroxocobalamin because, unlike nitrites, it doesn't ↓ oxygen-carrying capacity; MSD calls this concern probably overstated
claims.quote: Cyanide casualties resulting from smoke inhalation may also have carbon monoxide poisoning. In such cases, hydroxycobalamin has been recommended over nitrates by some authorities because, unlike nitrites, hydroxycobalamin does not decrease oxygen-carrying capacity (3, 4). However, concerns about administering nitrites in this situation are probably overstated.
